Southeast.text: Spot cotton trading was moderate. Supplies and producer offerings were light. Demand was moderate. Average local spot prices were higher. Trading of CCC-loan equities was inactive. Dry and sunny weather dominated the weather pattern across the lower Southeast this week with mild afternoon temperatures prevailing throughout the period. Daytime high temperatures were mostly in the 60s and 70s. Nighttime lows were in the upper 40s to mid-50s. Around one-half to one inch of precipitation was received in the far western Florida Peninsula during the week. Elsewhere, mostly dry conditions persisted. Defoliation and harvest activities advanced without interruption. According to the National Agricultural Statistics Service's (NASS) Crop Progress report released October 19, bolls opening advanced to 93 percent in Georgia and 90 percent in Alabama. Harvesting advanced to 38 percent completed in Alabama and 26 percent in Georgia. Sunny and warm conditions prevailed across the upper Southeast during the period. Daytime high temperatures were in the 60s and 70s. Nighttime lows were in the 40s. Widespread showers brought light moisture to areas across North Carolina and coastal Virginia. Rainfall totals measured from around one-half to one inch of moisture. The moisture helped ease short-term moisture deficits across areas of Virginia and the Carolinas, according to the U.S. Drought Monitor. Defoliation and harvesting activities advanced as dry conditions allowed. According to NASS, harvesting advanced to 27 percent completed in Virginia and 16 percent in the Carolinas.

North Delta.text: Trading of spot cotton and CCC-loan equities was inactive. Supplies of available cotton were light. Demand was light Average local spot prices were firm. No forward contracting was reported. Industry participants monitored cotton prices throughout the period, hoping for any indication of a modest upward movement. Scattered rainfall moved into the region on Friday, October 16, lowering daytime high temperatures into the 60s. Sunny conditions persisted throughout most of the reporting period and raised daytime highs back into the 70s and 80s. Nighttime lows ranged from the 40s to the 50s. Accumulated precipitation totals varied from trace amounts up to around one-quarter of an inch. In the Bootheel and Mid-South regions, field activities continued as producers worked to harvest the remaining cotton acres. Modules were transported by truck to gins, and ginning facilities operated multiple shifts to accommodate incoming seed cotton supplies. According to the National Agricultural Statistics Service's (NASS) Crop Progress report released October 19, harvest progress reached 63 percent complete in Arkansas, 42 in Missouri, and 46 percent in Tennessee.

South Delta.text: Spot cotton trading was inactive. Supplies of available cotton were light. Demand was light. Average local spot prices were firm. Trading of CCC-loan equities was inactive. No forward contracting was reported. Mostly sunny skies dominated the weather pattern throughout the reporting period. Daytime high temperatures in the 60s over the weekend reached the 70s and 80s by the end of the week. Nighttime lows ranged from the 30s to the 50s. No precipitation was reported during the period. A slow-soaking rain was needed to restore moisture to the soil. Harvesting activities continued to near completion. According to the National Agricultural Statistics Service's (NASS) Crop Progress report released on October 19, cotton harvest reached 72 percent in Louisiana and 70 percent in Mississippi. Both states were closely aligned in progress and remained well ahead of the five-year average percentages. Ginning continued to gain momentum as additional facilities began operating on 24-hour shifts. Warehouses were receiving cotton from gins and shipping orders.

East Texas-South Texas.text: Spot cotton trading was active. Supplies and producer offerings were moderate. Demand was light. Average local spot prices were firm. Trading of CCC-loan equities was inactive. Forward contracting activity was inactive. Foreign mill inquiries were light. Inquiries were best from Korea, Pakistan, and Vietnam. In East Texas, clear and sunny weather conditions prevailed as a cold front entered the region bringing in cooler, fall-like temperatures. Daytime highs peaked in the mid-80s, with nighttime lows dipping into 40s and 50s. Spotty showers produced only minimal rainfall accumulations. Harvest activities continued but were nearing completion. Unharvested fields were ready to be defoliated, or some producers were expected to wait on the first freeze to begin the process of leaf desiccation. Modules were transported to gin yards. Gins continued working through backlogs of modules. In South Texas, partly cloudy skies and slightly cooler temperatures prevailed. Daytime high temperatures were in the 70s to the 80s, and nighttime low temperatures dropped into the 50s before warming back up into the 70s as the week progressed. No rainfall was reported. Ginning operations continued in the South Texas region and were wrapped up in the Rio Grande Valley. Gins in the Upper Coast and Coastal Bend regions continued to work through modules on gin yards.

West Texas-Kansas-Oklahoma.text: Spot cotton trading was slow. Supplies and producer offerings were moderate. Demand was light. Average local spot prices were higher. Producer interest in forward contracting was light. Trading of CCC-loan equities was inactive. Foreign mill inquiries were light. Interest was best from Korea, Pakistan, and Vietnam. Mid-week warm and sunny harvest weather turned cooler and damp across the West Texas region. Daytime highs ranged from the mid-50s to the mid-80s, while nighttime temperatures transitioned from the 30s to the 60s. Several locations recorded the first freeze or frost of the season before overnight temperatures returned to more seasonable levels. The brief, intermittent showers were welcomed but untimely, especially with additional rain in the forecast. Spraying defoliants and harvest activities expanded and made good progress as soils firmed following last period's historic rainfall. Concerns surfaced regarding fiber quality and regrowth that made desiccation difficult. Modules were transported to gin yards, and more gins began pressing operations, with a few expanding operating hours. Insurance adjusters evaluated field progress and made determinations as production estimates continued to decline. Daytime temperatures in Kansas ranged from the upper 50s to the lower 80s, while nighttime lows dipped into the lower 30s and the upper 50s. Harvesting activities resumed at some locations once fields dried enough to support heavy machinery following recent, welcomed but untimely rainfall. Spraying progressed slowly in areas that had received heavier precipitation in the previous reporting period. Ginning was underway at some sites. Harvest activities were slow to advance across Oklahoma after rainy weather caused interruptions, but fields were firming and a significant number of acres were expected to be harvested over the upcoming weekend. Daytime temperatures ranged from the lower 60s to the lower 80s, and overnight lows dipped into the upper 30s to the 50s. Ginning and module hauling were inconvenienced by saturated gin yards, and a handful of gins decided not to open operations.

Desert Southwest (DSW).text: Spot cotton trading was inactive. Supplies and producer offerings were light. Demand was light. No forward contracting was reported during the period. Average local prices were firm. Foreign mill inquiries were light. Partly cloudy skies with light showers early in the week in Arizona transitioned into more severe weather as the week progressed, including flash flooding, tornadoes, and hailstorms in central Arizona. Other areas of the DSW received mostly cloudy conditions with chances for rainfall later in the period. This type of severe weather is unusual for Arizona, and damage was reported to power lines and homes in some of the cotton-growing areas of the state. Damage assessments will be ongoing to determine what damage, if any, was done to the crop. Daytime temperatures ranged from the upper 70s to the 80s and up into the 90s in Yuma, AZ. Nighttime lows were in the 50s to 70s. Ginning continued in Yuma, AZ.

American Pima (AP).text: Spot cotton trading was inactive. Supplies were moderate. Demand was light. No forward contracting or domestic mill activity was reported. Average local spot prices were steady. Mill inquiries were light. In Arizona, severe weather including flash flooding, tornadoes, and hail activity was reported. Daytime highs ranged from the 60s to the 90s across the Far Western region, while nighttime lows cooled into the 50s and 70s. In central Arizona, damage was reported to power lines and homes in some of the cotton-growing areas of the state, including Overgaard, AZ. As a result, damage assessments will be made to determine what damage, if any, was done to the crop. In other parts of the region, the crop advanced steadily, and some areas expanded picker harvesting. Ginning continued in Yuma, AZ. In the SJV, harvest was expanding in Tulare and Kern Counties in California. Gins increased operations to accommodate accumulating modules on gin yards.
